subject: Next steps: Procurement & PR guidance for Redwood inference
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@acme-corp.com>, Mark Davenport <mdavenport@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Next steps from today's discovery – procurement & PR path

Hi Alyssa / Mark,

Thanks again for taking the time today — really appreciate the openness on requirements and the clear constraints from procurement. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we don't lose momentum: 

- Procurement readiness: you mentioned Acme uses Coupa for supplier onboarding and Ariba for PO management in some BU pockets.
- Commercial path: Acme prefers PO for enterprise purchases but also supports corporate card for small pilot purchases.
- Immediate asks from your team: supplier setup form (for Coupa), supplier ID if already onboarded, and confirmation on whether a Purchase Requisition (PR) needs to be raised first or we can proceed with a card for the pilot.

Suggested next steps:
1) Alyssa / Procurement: send the Coupa supplier setup form and indicate whether Redwood is already in your system (supplier ID if available).
2) Marissa (me): share Redwood's supplier info and SOW/contract template for procurement review.
3) Internal (Rishi / Dev): once supplier ID & PR path confirmed, we'll prepare an internal mutual action plan and provide any required invoice/payment terms.

Can you confirm the above and share the supplier setup form? If Acme needs a PR to be created by your side, please share the PR creation timeline and internal ticketing ID (Coupa/Ariba request) so we can align contracting timelines.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 15-min follow-up if that helps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_sow_template.docx (DOCX, 34 KB)

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Mark Davenport <mdavenport@acme-corp.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme-corp.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Next steps from today's discovery – procurement & PR path

Marissa, thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers from procurement: 

- We do use Coupa for supplier setup across the company; some of our regional teams submit POs through Ariba as well.
- For deals of this size, our standard path is: supplier onboarding in Coupa -> PR created by the BU (shows up in Ariba for some teams) -> PO issued.
- For pilots under $10k, we can consider a corporate card, but procurement needs the business justification and an approved PR for anything that converts to a longer-term contract.

I've attached the Coupa supplier setup form and our supplier checklist. Please complete and return; procurement will then kick off onboarding.

Also FYI our procurement team prefers to have a Supplier Diversity and W-9 on file — included in the checklist.

Coupa ticketing: we've created an internal ticket (ACME-PR-4012) to track the onboarding. I'll update you once Redwood is assigned a supplier ID.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Sr. Program Manager, AI Integrations
Alyssa.Chen@acme-corp.com

Attachments: acme_supplier_setup_form.pdf (PDF, 42 KB); acme_supplier_checklist.xlsx (XLSX, 12 KB)

Looping you both in — procurement at Acme has opened Coupa ticket ACME-PR-4012 and attached their supplier setup form (see Alyssa's reply below).

Ask for Dev: can you confirm what Redwood needs to complete the supplier setup form (tax IDs, bank details, sample invoice template) and help populate any technical fields on the form? If useful I can schedule 20m with Alyssa and procurement to walk through.

Ask for Rishi: once we have the supplier ID / PR path, can you prepare a short mutual action plan that calls out the pilot scope, expected start date, and billing terms so procurement has a clear business justification? We should also surface the card option for the pilot (<$10k) as a contingency to accelerate rollout.

I'll attach our SOW template and a one-page payment terms doc to share with procurement.

Thanks — we want to avoid delays once the supplier onboarding completes.

Best,
Marissa Cole
